answer: DeepWalk uses the PPI (protein-protein interaction) network as a benchmark because it is a standard graph-embedding testbed with rich, real-world network structure and widely used node labels, so it lets researchers evaluate whether the method can learn useful latent representations from graph topology. In the blogger-interest setting, the idea is that if DeepWalk can capture structural similarity in one network, it may also produce embeddings that help predict attributes or interests in another social network. However, using the PPI network does not directly model social ties, so it is not a perfect proxy for social relationships. As a result, performance on social-relationship tasks depends on how well the structural patterns learned from PPI transfer; DeepWalk can still perform well because it learns neighborhood-based embeddings, but the benchmark choice mainly demonstrates general graph representation ability rather than being tailored specifically to social link prediction.
